topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text: I stepped into the classroom, the air thick with unspoken words. I looked at the student, their eyes wide, shoulders a little too tense. "I believe in you," I found myself saying, though no one had spoken of doubt. The room seemed to soften around me, the hard edges of accusation melting away. I asked them to share their story, to walk me through the paper, the ideas, the journey of their mind. We talked about sources, about voices echoing through pages, how sometimes a whisper from a book becomes our own shout. It’s a dance, a conversation, and I wanted them to know they were not alone in it. We ended the session with a plan, a few steps to tighten the cords of their scholarship, to weave their unique voice even more firmly into their work. The student left, a bit lighter, the weight of the room lifted, carried away by the promise of fresh beginnings.
